ledger.note: 138: a Han fleet from Kuaiji makes Minyue withdraw. The Emperor Wu page: the Kuaiji governor was coerced 'to mobilize a large naval fleet to Dong'ou's rescue' and 'Minyue forces became fearful and retreated'; the Dong'ou infobox says 'Defeated by Minyue: 138 BC' and its text has the Dong'ou king submit. 135: Minyue invades Nanyue. 'In 135 BC, Minyue saw an opportunity to take advantage of the new and inexperienced king of Nanyue, Zhao Mo'; the Minyue text says 'In 137 BC, Minyue invaded Nanyue'. Neither names a route; the zone is the band along the Minyue-Nanyue frontier of Cliopatria's 126 shapes, the researcher's reading.

135: the invasion ends in a murder and a peace. 'the Minyue king was murdered by his brother Zou Yushan, who sued for peace with the Han'; the Han enthroned Zou Wuzhu's grandson Zou Chou as king and recognised Zou Yushan as king of Dongyue. No land changed hands on the page; the Emperor Wu page has Nanyue ask Han for help and the Minyue king assassinated by nobles.

135: the Han divide the kingdom between two kings, Minyue and Dongyue. Infobox 'Divided by the Han dynasty among the Minyue king and the Dongyue king: 135 BC'; Emperor Wu page: 'Dongyue (東越) was ruled by Luo Yushan' and 'Minyue was split into a dual monarchy'; Minyue page: 'recognized him as king of Dongyue instead of ordering a second invasion'. No page opened (Minyue, Emperor Wu of Han, History of Fujian, Baiyue, Kuaiji Commandery) names any land for either king, so the region is the whole kingdom that was divided, not Dongyue's share, and the Minyue keyframes are not reduced after 135: the dongyue dossier (to be written) must say which part of this shape Luo Yushan held. The date is the infobox's (confidence 3 for the date, 2 here for the land). Fix of request R005 (3 Nov 2026): the split now names no land (its region is the kingdom minus itself, which the compiler skips as an event that moves no land), because the Dongyue dossier does not exist and the split emptied 680 cells for nine years. Minyue page, infobox 'Divided by the Han dynasty among the Minyue king and the Dongyue king: 135 BC': 'As a result, there were two kings coexisting in the country'; Zou Yushan was recognised 'king of Dongyue instead of ordering a second invasion'; the page names no territory, region, city or boundary for either king. The dossier keeps both kings' land as Minyue to 110. A Dongyue dossier, if one is written, must say which part of the kingdom Zou Yushan held (handoff).

minus.text: Dong'ou, 'an ancient kingdom in modern Wenzhou and Taizhou, Zhejiang Province, China' (Dong'ou page)

zones.text: Wuzhu's kingdom without Dong'ou (Wenzhou and Taizhou), which Emperor Gaozu gave to Zou Yao in 192. 'His kingdom extended beyond the borders of contemporary Fujian into eastern Guangdong, eastern Jiangxi, and southern Zhejiang.' (History of Fujian)

wars.outcome: Han forces 'approached Minyue simultaneously from four directions via land and sea in 111 BC'; Zou Yushan was murdered, the rulers surrendered, Han annexed Minyue and Dongyue (110 on the Minyue infobox and the Emperor Wu page) and moved the people to the Yangtze-Huai region.
wars.note: The Minyue page also has Nanyue rebelling in 112 and Yang Pu asking leave to attack Zou Yushan; Emperor Wu 'felt it was too much trouble to occupy Minyue, as it was a region full of narrow mountain passes'.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier. Fujian is bounded by the sea and mountains; the Guangdong, Jiangxi and southern-Zhejiang edges are Cliopatria's and approximate.

Pages opened, first pass: Minyue, Qin dynasty, Qin's wars of unification, Dong'ou, History of Fujian (budget 5, all used) and Emperor Wu of Han (a sixth, opened for the dong-ou dossier). SAME OR DIFFERENT STATE: Minyue (Q1936158) shares its Wikidata id with Yue (-500..-334, the yue dossier). They are different states: Yue is the Spring and Autumn kingdom of Goujian that Chu and Qi destroyed; Minyue is the kingdom of its refugee family in Fujian. This is one dossier, cliopatria_names ['Minyue'].

SECOND PASS, WHAT CHANGED (review finding, then action):
1. Southern Zhejiang. The History of Fujian says of Wuzhu: 'His kingdom extended beyond the borders of contemporary Fujian into eastern Guangdong, eastern Jiangxi, and southern Zhejiang.' (three fetches gave the comma before 'and'; the reviewer's fetch rendered it without; the words are the same.) The first pass cut the quote and dropped Zhejiang. Now: the quote is whole everywhere; southern Zhejiang is added to Wuzhu's kingdom from 206 as the 340 Zhejiang cells (27.3-29.9 N) of Cliopatria's 206 shape; the 203 shape's other 140 Zhejiang cells (29.5-31.2 N) stay cut, as do Anhui, Hubei, Jiangsu, Hunan and the Jiangxi beyond the 202 shape. The pre-Qin shape (306-223) and the Qin-occupied shapes (214-206) still have no Zhejiang: the page gives the extent for Wuzhu's kingdom only, and Qin's Kuaiji Commandery held the Wuyue land from 222 (Qin's wars page, 'citation needed'). The 206-203 years rest on Cliopatria alone, since the page dates only 202. I did not take the reviewer's second option (southern Zhejiang means Dong'ou's land only): Dong'ou's discs are 77 of the 340 cells, and the History of Fujian names no Zhejiang kingdom beside Minyue.
2. Dong'ou. New split event 192 (counterpart dong-ou) and new keyframe minyue_-192: Wenzhou and Taizhou leave Wuzhu's kingdom for Zou Yao ('The realm of Dong'ou was given to Zou Yao by Emperor Gaozu of Han in 192 BC', Dong'ou page; Minyue page: 'and in 192 BC, he made Zou Yao king of Dong'ou (Eastern Ou).'). Confidence 2: that the land had been Minyue's is my reading of 'southern Zhejiang'; the Dong'ou page does not say. The rest of southern Zhejiang (263 cells) stays Minyue's to 110. Who held Wenzhou and Taizhou after the 138 submission: the Kuaiji Commandery page is silent; the Baiyue page has the Dong'ou people 'settled in the region between the Yangtze and Huai River'; dong-ou gives the land to han-dynasty in 138 (conf 2).
3. 135. The rename is now a split, counterpart dongyue. No page names a Dongyue land (Minyue, Emperor Wu, History of Fujian, Baiyue, Kuaiji Commandery all silent), so the region is the whole kingdom that was divided and the shape is not reduced after 135; the dongyue owner must say which part Luo Yushan held. If a renderer reads the split literally it would move the whole region: treat it as a caption event until dongyue exists.
4. 202. The rename is dropped (no name or dynasty changed: 'he restored Minyue's status as a tributary independent kingdom'); the caption is in the minyue_-202 keyframe note; han-dynasty owes vassal_start 202 / vassal_end 110, counterpart minyue.
5. Quotes. The ledger notes for 110 now quote the Dong'ou page word for word ('the aspiration for autonomous control over Dongyue gradually dissipated during the final months of 111 BC'; 'prompting the Han dynasty to eventually incorporate Dongyue and the remaining territories of the former Minyue') and the Emperor Wu page ('assassinated him and surrendered the kingdom to Han'); the Dong'ou location quote is now 'an ancient kingdom in modern Wenzhou and Taizhou, Zhejiang Province, China'.
6. Thin items tried, still silent: end of the Qin occupation 206 (Chu-Han Contention does not mention Minyue, Fujian or the southern commanderies; the Minyue page has only 'When the Qin dynasty fell in 206 BC, the Hegemon-King Xiang Yu did not make Zou Wuzhu and Zou Yao kings', so the event stays confidence 1 and now cites that sentence). Fujian in 333-307: the Yue (state) page has 'Yue was conquered by Chu in 333 BC' and the family moving to northern Fujian and setting up Minyue, undated; nothing names a state or ruler of Fujian before 306, so 306 stays (infobox, History of Fujian) and the 27-year gap with the yue dossier remains. The yue dossier gives minyue as successor with 'Cliopatria's Minyue row from 333' (Zhejiang included): that is the yue owner's to re-route.

DISAGREEMENTS KEPT: start 306 (infobox, lead, History of Fujian) against 334 (Minyue text) against 333 (Cliopatria; Yue page for Yue's fall). End 110 (infobox, lead, Emperor Wu) against 111 (History of Fujian, Dong'ou page campaign dates, Cliopatria): 110 used, minyue_-110 added. Invasion of Nanyue 135 (Emperor Wu, infobox division date) against 137 (Minyue text): 135 used. The pages name the co-kings differently (Zou Yushan and Zou Chou; Luo Yushan and Luo Jugu). Qin status: annexed (Minzhong Commandery) against vassal ('a vassal of the Qin Empire for over a decade'): drawn as occupation 214-206.

CLIOPATRIA SHAPES: far too large before Qin (all of Zhejiang) and in 206-203 (Anhui, Hubei, northern Zhejiang, extra Jiangxi: no page); too small at the Fujian coast from 212 (88 cells incl. Fuzhou); absent 170-127. The corrected shape (Fujian, the 202 shape's Guangdong and Jiangxi, southern Zhejiang) is about 405,000 km2 on the grid (1,602 cells; 1,525 without Dong'ou). The infobox gives no area (population 400,000 in 110 BC), so no ratio.

NOT ON ANY PAGE OPENED: Wuzhu's reign dates, the date of the Minzhong Commandery, which land Dongyue held, who held Wenzhou and Taizhou 137-111, what Minyue gained in 138 (Dong'ou's land does not appear in later Cliopatria shapes), the 154 BC revolt's effect on Minyue ('The king of Minyue refused'), Cliopatria's 206-203 extent.
